title: AI in Excel 2: Agent Mode, Plan and verification

lessons.title: Chat, Plan and Edit modes, and choosing a model
learn: OpenAI vs Anthropic models in Copilot

steps.say: Here's the finished sheet. Twenty expense claims, a policy table, and a Within policy column that Copilot added in Edit mode. On the right, a note of which mode we used for each step. Picking the right mode keeps your file safe.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S19-01 Done

steps.say: You'll learn what Chat, Plan and Edit modes can change, when to use each, and how to choose between OpenAI and Anthropic models in Copilot. Practice sheet: S19-01.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Chat mode: answers, no changes
• Edit mode (Agent Mode): changes the workbook
• Plan mode: shows the steps before editing
• Choosing a model: OpenAI or Anthropic
Practice sheet: S19-01

steps.say: Think of the three modes as three levels of permission. Chat reads and answers. Plan proposes steps and waits for you. Edit goes ahead and changes cells, sheets and formulas.

acts.t:
Copilot modes in Excel
Chat: reads and answers. Nothing on the sheet changes.
Plan: writes a step-by-step plan, you approve or change it.
Edit (Agent Mode): builds and edits sheets, formulas, charts.
All three need the file on OneDrive with AutoSave on.

steps.say: Open sheet S19-01. The claims are in A1 to F21, and the policy limits per claim are in I1 to J5.
Open Copilot and choose Chat mode. Ask: which department has the highest total Travel spend? Do not change anything.

acts.t: Which Department has the highest total Amount for the Travel category? Do not change anything.

steps.say: Copilot answers in the pane. Look at the sheet: nothing changed. That's what Chat mode is for. Quick questions, explanations and ideas, with no risk to your data.
Now switch to Edit mode. Type: add a column Within policy that shows Yes if Amount is less than or equal to the limit for its Category in I1 to J5, otherwise No.

acts.t: Add a column called Within policy that shows Yes if Amount is less than or equal to the limit for its Category in the table I1:J5, otherwise No.

steps.say: This time the sheet changes. Copilot adds the new column with a formula. Click the first cell of the new column and read the formula bar. It should compare the amount with a lookup of the category's limit.
Now check it. In J8, type equals SUMPRODUCT, open bracket, two minus signs, open bracket, F2 colon F21, greater than, SUMIFS of J2 colon J5, I2 colon I5, D2 colon D21, then close all brackets.
J8 shows 8. That's how many claims break the policy. Count the No answers in Copilot's column. They should be the same.
Now Plan mode. Ask: plan how you would add a summary of claims by Department and Category on a new sheet. Copilot shows the steps first and waits for you.

acts.t: Plan how you would add a summary of total claims by Department and Category on a new sheet, with a total row.

steps.say: Read the plan. Each step says what Copilot intends to do. Nothing has changed yet. We'll approve and edit plans in a later lesson, so for now, leave it.
Last, the model. At the bottom of the Copilot pane there's a model picker. Auto lets Microsoft choose. You can also pick an OpenAI model or an Anthropic Claude model. Your company may limit the list.

acts.t:
Choosing a model in Copilot
• Model picker at the bottom of the Copilot pane
• Auto: Microsoft picks per task
• OpenAI (GPT) or Anthropic (Claude) models
• Try the same prompt on two models when an answer looks weak
• Your admin may hide some models

steps.say: When does the model matter? For short questions, rarely. For long multi-step builds, results differ. If one model's formulas look clumsy, run the same prompt with the other and compare.

acts.t:
Practical rule
Same prompt, two models, compare:
• Are the formulas readable?
• Did it follow every instruction?
• Do the totals match your own check?

steps.say: A common mistake is asking a question in Edit mode. Copilot may change your sheet to answer it, for example by adding a helper column you didn't want. Use Chat for questions.

acts.t:
Common mistake
Asking “Which department spends most?” in Edit mode.
Copilot may add columns or sheets to answer.
Questions → Chat. Changes → Edit. Big changes → Plan first.

steps.say: To recap. Chat answers without editing. Edit changes the workbook, so read what it wrote. Plan shows the steps first. And the model picker lets you compare OpenAI and Anthropic.

acts.t:
Recap
• Chat: questions, no changes
• Edit: changes, then read and check
• Plan: approve steps before changes
• Model picker: compare when results look weak

steps.say: Your challenge: in Chat mode ask which employee has the most claims over the limit, then check it with COUNTIFS on the Within policy column. Compare with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Chat mode: which Employee has the most claims over the limit?
Check with COUNTIFS on the Within policy column.
Compare with sheet S19-01 Done.

lessons.title: Agent Mode: build a dashboard from one prompt

steps.say: This is a sales dashboard: four KPI cards, revenue by region, a monthly trend and sales rep rankings, all driven by formulas on the SalesData table. Agent Mode can build a first version of this from one prompt.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S19-02 Done

steps.say: You'll learn to write a multi-step goal for Agent Mode, review what it built, and prove the dashboard refreshes when new data arrives. Practice sheet: S19-02.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Write one prompt with a clear multi-step goal
• Review every sheet, formula and chart it builds
• Add new data and watch the dashboard update
Practice sheet: S19-02

steps.say: A good Agent Mode prompt reads like a brief to a junior colleague. Say the goal, the source table, every item you want, where to put it, and one rule: use formulas that refer to the table.

acts.t:
Agent Mode prompt recipe
Goal: a sales dashboard for FY 2025-26
Data: the SalesData table
Items: KPIs, charts, top 5 reps
Where: a new sheet called Dashboard
Rule: formulas linked to the table, no pasted values

steps.say: Open sheet S19-02. One hundred sales rows sit in a table called SalesData, from A1 to H101.

Open Copilot in Edit mode and paste the brief. Build a sales dashboard on a new sheet called Dashboard, with KPI cards, a monthly trend chart, revenue by region and the top five sales reps, all as formulas on the SalesData table.

acts.t: Build a sales dashboard on a new sheet called Dashboard. Include KPI cards for total Revenue, gross margin % (1 minus Cost divided by Revenue) and number of orders, a line chart of monthly Revenue, a column chart of Revenue by Region, and a table of the top 5 Sales reps by Revenue. Use formulas that refer to the SalesData table so everything updates when data changes. Do not paste values.

steps.say: Agent Mode works through the steps one by one, and you can watch the pane list what it's doing. It may create helper tables, then charts, then format the sheet. This can take a minute.
Let's review what it built. Go to the Dashboard sheet. Look at the KPI cards first, then the charts. The exact layout will be different each time you run the prompt.
Click the total revenue card and read the formula bar. You want to see a reference to SalesData, Revenue, not a typed number. A typed number won't update.
Now check the AI's work. Go back to sheet S19-02. In J2 type equals SUM, open bracket, SalesData, open square bracket, Revenue, close square bracket, close bracket.
J2 shows ₹2,11,57,900. Compare it with the total revenue card on the Dashboard. If they differ, ask Copilot which rows its formula uses.
Also check one region. In J5 type equals SUMIFS, open bracket, SalesData Revenue, comma, SalesData Region, comma, quote West quote, close bracket.
J5 shows ₹45,06,900. That should match the West bar on the region chart.

Now prove it refreshes. Click A102, the first empty row under the table, and type a new sale: 31 March 2026, West, Maharashtra, Refrigerator, Rohan Mehta, eight units, two lakh fifty thousand rupees revenue, one lakh eighty-five thousand cost. Press Tab between cells.
The table grew by one row automatically. J2 now shows ₹2,14,07,900, up by two and a half lakh.

Go to the Dashboard. The revenue card, the West bar and March in the trend line should all be higher. If something didn't move, that item was built from pasted values, and you should ask Copilot to rebuild it with formulas.
A common mistake is a vague prompt like: make a dashboard. You get something, but not what your manager wanted. List every KPI and chart, and name the sheet.

acts.t:
Common mistake
Vague: “Make a dashboard.”
Better: name the sheet, list each KPI and chart, say “use formulas linked to SalesData”.
Then follow up: “Add a slicer for Region”, “Use our colours”.

steps.say: A pro tip: after Agent Mode finishes, ask it to list every formula it created and where. That gives you a checklist to review instead of hunting around the sheet.

acts.t: List every formula you created on the Dashboard sheet with its cell address and what it calculates.

steps.say: To recap. Give Agent Mode a full brief in one prompt. Review the sheets and formulas it creates. And add a test row to prove the dashboard updates.

acts.t:
Recap
• One prompt: goal, data, items, place, rule
• Review: formulas, not typed numbers
• Test: add a row, totals and charts move

steps.say: Your challenge: ask Agent Mode to add a Region slicer and a KPI card for average units per order, then check the new card with your own formula. Compare with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Ask Agent Mode: add a Region slicer and a KPI card for average Units per order.
Check it: =SUM(SalesData[Units])/ROWS(SalesData[Units])
Compare with sheet S19-02 Done.

lessons.title: Plan mode: review before Copilot edits

steps.say: Here's the finished vendor ageing report: unpaid invoices sorted into 0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and over 90 days, with the old ones in red. We built it with Plan mode, so we approved every step before Copilot touched the file.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S19-03 Done

steps.say: You'll learn to ask for a plan, change a step before approving, and undo or review what Copilot changed. Practice sheet: S19-03.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Ask Copilot for a plan first
• Approve, change or reject steps
• Undo and review Copilot's changes
Practice sheet: S19-03

steps.say: Plan mode is for bigger jobs where a wrong guess is expensive, like finance reports. Copilot lists its steps. You edit them in plain English. Only then does it build.

acts.t:
Plan mode workflow
1. Describe the goal
2. Copilot proposes numbered steps
3. You reply: change step 2, drop step 4…
4. Approve, and Copilot carries out the plan
5. Review, undo with Command Z if needed

steps.say: Open sheet S19-03. Twenty-five vendor invoices are in A1 to G26, with GSTINs, invoice and due dates, amounts and status. The as-of date, 31 March 2026, is in L1.
Open Copilot in Plan mode and describe the report: an ageing of unpaid invoices on a new sheet, in four buckets, with totals by vendor and anything over ninety days highlighted.

acts.t: Create an ageing report of the Unpaid invoices on a new sheet called Ageing: days overdue = as-of date minus Due date, buckets 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and Over 90, a table of totals by Vendor and bucket, and highlight Over 90 in red.

steps.say: Copilot replies with a numbered plan. Read every step. Look for the as-of date in particular. Many plans use today's date, which would change the report every day.
Change the step you don't like. Type: use the as-of date in cell L1 of sheet S19-03, not today's date, so I can change it later.

acts.t: Change the plan: use the as-of date in cell L1 of sheet S19-03, not today's date, so I can change it later. Show me the updated plan.

steps.say: Check the updated plan mentions L1. If it does, approve it.
Type: looks good, go ahead with the updated plan. Copilot now builds the report step by step.

acts.t: Looks good. Go ahead with the updated plan.

steps.say: Go to the new Ageing sheet. Look at the bucket totals and the red highlights. The layout will vary, but there should be four buckets and only unpaid invoices.
Now check it. Back on sheet S19-03, in L3 type equals SUMIFS, open bracket, F2 colon F26, comma, G2 colon G26, comma, quote Unpaid quote, close bracket.
L3 shows ₹35,62,800. The four buckets on the Ageing sheet should add up to exactly this.
Now the over-ninety bucket. In L4 type equals SUMIFS, F2 colon F26, G2 colon G26, quote Unpaid quote, then E2 colon E26 with the condition: less than, ampersand, L1 minus 90.
L4 shows ₹23,37,700. Compare it with the Over 90 bucket. If they match, the plan was carried out correctly.
If you don't like a change, undo it. Press Command Z to step back through Copilot's edits, and Command Y to redo. In the Copilot pane you can also review the list of changes it made.

A common mistake is approving a plan without reading it. The usual culprits are today's date, the wrong status filter, or a step that overwrites your source data. Thirty seconds of reading saves an hour of fixing.

acts.t:
Common mistake
Approving without reading. Watch for:
• TODAY() instead of your as-of date
• Paid invoices included by mistake
• A step that edits or sorts the source table
• A step you didn't ask for

steps.say: To recap. Plan mode shows the steps first. You change steps in plain English before approving. And after it runs, check the totals and undo with Command Z if needed.

acts.t:
Recap
• Plan mode: steps first, changes later
• Edit the plan in plain English, then approve
• Check totals; Command Z undoes, Command Y redoes

steps.say: Your challenge: change the as-of date in L1 to 30 June 2026 and check that the Ageing sheet updates. Then recompute the over-ninety total with SUMIFS. Compare with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Change L1 to 30-06-2026.
Does the Ageing sheet move invoices into older buckets?
Recheck Over 90 with SUMIFS.
Compare with sheet S19-03 Done.

lessons.title: Checking AI work
learn: Read every formula the AI wrote
lessons.mac:
Show Formulas: Control + ` (backtick, above Tab)
Excel for Mac: Formulas tab > Trace Precedents draws arrows
to every cell a formula uses

steps.say: Here's the corrected summary. Last week an AI assistant built five summary formulas for this GST register, and two of them were wrong. One missed the last invoice, and one used a typed count. Both looked fine at a glance.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S19-05 Done

steps.say: You'll learn a short routine for checking any AI output: recompute a key total by hand, read every formula, and ask the AI to audit itself. Practice sheet: S19-05.

acts.t:
You will learn
• Recompute one key total by hand
• Read every formula the AI wrote (Show Formulas)
• Look for short ranges and typed numbers
• Ask Copilot to review, then decide yourself
Practice sheet: S19-05

steps.say: Here's the routine. Totals first, then formulas, then edge cases. It takes two minutes and catches most problems.

acts.t:
The 3-step check
1. Totals: recompute one or two key numbers yourself
2. Formulas: read each one; do the ranges cover all rows?
3. Edge cases: blanks, last row, a typed number, a filter left on

steps.say: Open sheet S19-05. Twenty tax invoices are in A1 to F21. The AI-built summary is in H1 to I6.
Step one, totals. In K2 type equals SUM, open bracket, D2 colon D21, close bracket. This is your own total of taxable value.
K2 shows ₹45,01,900, but the AI's figure in I2 shows ₹40,89,400. They don't match. Something is wrong.
Step two, read the formula. With I2 selected, look at the formula bar. It says SUM of D2 to D20. Row 21, the last invoice, is missing. That's four lakh twelve thousand five hundred rupees.
To read all the formulas at once, go to the Formulas tab and click Show Formulas. Every cell now shows its formula instead of its value.

Read down the list. I3 covers all twenty rows. I4 adds two cells. But I5 divides by 19, a typed number. There are twenty invoices, so the average is wrong too, and it won't update if you add an invoice.
Turn Show Formulas off again. Then ask Copilot to review. In Chat mode, type: check the formulas in I2 to I6 for errors, wrong ranges and hard-coded numbers. Don't change anything.

acts.t: Check the formulas in I2:I6 for errors, ranges that miss rows, and hard-coded numbers. Do not change anything; list each problem with its cell.

steps.say: Copilot lists what it found. Compare its list with what you found. AI reviewers are useful, but they can miss things or flag things that are fine, so your own check comes first.
Now fix I2. Click I2, type equals SUM, open bracket, D2 colon D21, close bracket, and press Return.
Fix I5. Type equals I4 divided by COUNTA, open bracket, A2 colon A21, close bracket. Now the count comes from the data.
I2 now matches your total of ₹45,01,900, and I5 shows ₹2,49,392. As a final check, in K5 type equals AVERAGE of D2 to D21 plus AVERAGE of F2 to F21. It should match I5.
Why does this matter so much? AI answers vary between runs, and a short range or typed number gives no error. The sheet looks normal. Only a check catches it.

acts.t:
Common mistake
Trusting a number because there's no error.
• Short ranges and typed numbers never show #REF! or #VALUE!
• They break silently when data grows
• A hand total is the fastest way to catch them

steps.say: On a Mac, Show Formulas is Control plus the backtick key, the key above Tab. On Excel for Mac you can also use Formulas, Trace Precedents to draw arrows to the cells a formula uses.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Show Formulas: Control + ` (backtick, above Tab)
Excel for Mac: Formulas tab > Trace Precedents draws arrows
to every cell a formula uses

steps.say: To recap. Recompute one key total yourself. Read every formula, looking for short ranges and typed numbers. And use Copilot's review as a second opinion, not the first.

acts.t:
Recap
• Hand-check one total, every time
• Show Formulas: read ranges and constants
• AI review is a second opinion; you sign off

steps.say: Your challenge: check I6, the Maharashtra total, with a filter or your own SUMIFS, and check I3 by multiplying a few rows by hand. Compare with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Check I6 (Maharashtra taxable value) your own way.
Check I3 (Total GST) against SUM of F2:F21.
Compare with sheet S19-05 Done.
